N3.claim: Under cumulative bans B_k = first k of [BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A*, greedy] on Qwen3-32B thinking, mechanistic compliance falls with k while lexical compliance stays high.
criteria: k=1: lexical and mechanistic compliance both >= 0.7
Jonckheere-Terpstra one-sided (decreasing in k) on binary mechanistic compliance over the 5 ordered groups: Monte-Carlo exact p (100,000 permutations) < 0.05; Cochran-Armitage beside
CONFIRMATION: held-out k=5 (W4/W5/P6/P7) gap >= 0.4 with Newcombe lower bound > 0
N3.denominators: among completed programs (primary) and over all samples
sensitivities: fine classes (e.g. greedy at k=4 is compliant)

N1.claim: Across the 10 retraced five-name-ban configurations, lexical compliance exceeds mechanistic compliance (gap = lex - mech, among traceable programs).
N1.primary: equal-weight mean of the 10 per-configuration gaps (95% configuration-cluster bootstrap, 10,000 resamples); program-weighted pooled gap beside it
N1.supported: pooled gap >= 0.3 AND gap > 0 in >= 7/10 configurations
N1.tests: per configuration: 2x2 lex x mech, Newcombe paired interval (method 10), exact McNemar on the discordant cells
sensitivities: untraceable counted as compliant (lower bound) and as non-compliant (upper bound)

N3-D.claim: exploratory: a name-free described five-mechanism ban vs the named k=5 cell
N3-D.direction: under R6, mechanistic compliance OR violation (banned class) rises relative to the named k=5 cell (unpaired Newcombe)
measures: lexical use of any banned name

N2.claim: Qwen3-32B-thinking's correct NAME-level survivors of the five-name ban mostly run a banned coarse order class.
N2.pool: iteration-8 screen 17 + held-out 21 + new A k=5 (W1-W3) + new A held-out
N2.supported: share in a banned coarse order class >= 0.6 (Wilson CI reported)
readings: (b) survivors whose name-level identity is not BFS order by definition (excluding unit Dijkstra, FIFO SPFA, wavefront/flood fill, uniform-cost search)
N2-adj: observed share minus the uniform-over-non-banned-catalogue null (0.6 coarse, 0.2 fine), Wilson interval shifted; the text states whether the share exceeds the null
N2.by_source: iteration-8 rows (cap 9,728) vs new rows (cap 12,288) reported separately

With only five algorithm centroids, the centroid-level Spearman of -0.63 cannot reach significance (p 0.133; the attainable floor is 0.033). A ban of five names is obeyed by name far more often than by mechanism. Read by runtime expansion order over 546 programs in ten configurations, lexical compliance exceeds mechanistic compliance by 0.70 (runtime label) or 0.61 (tracer), in every configuration, and in the three configurations with reasoning nearly every covert program comes with reasoning that names a banned algorithm; the tracer failed its gold gate on iterative deepening, so these numbers are descriptive. examples.output: No change of algorithm: under the entropy seed the grid task stays BFS 100 and shortest path Dijkstra 100, and in Qwen3-8B's later cell list both random seeds give Dijkstra 30 of 30 programs; the entropy seed stays within the paraphrase noise of the read-position state (0.734 and 1.165; on shortest path its 90% interval reaches 1.596, so equivalence was not shown there), and the word seed moves the grid state 1.555 times the noise without changing the program.

examples.input: 3 so how much does prompt instructions matter? ("Make a new algorithm", "Make a fully novel algorithm never seen before ... 2000 words ...")
examples.output: The long-form novelty instructions (about 2,000 words of design rationale before the code) produce claims of novelty, not new algorithms: of 574 outputs with a claim record, 484 (84%) claimed a new algorithm, and 220 of the 295 with code (75%) were catalogue algorithms; on shortest path the 2,000-word instruction gives Dijkstra 22 and Bellman-Ford/SPFA 6 correct programs of 30 in Qwen3-8B.

examples.input: hyp: is llm a probablistic model, and thus gives you the average/mean answer? and only context pushes you into a different subspace
examples.output: The instruct default is a sharpened choice of the base model, not its mean answer: on the three collapsed Qwen3-8B tasks the instruct fork margin exceeds the base model's by 2.1 to 13.4 nats while phrasing entropy moves by under 0.5 nats; in Gemma the grid fork gains 1.78 nats and post-training reversed and concentrated the base model's preference (base P(BFS) 0.25, 0.663 of base mass unmapped).

examples.input: logit lens / j-lens
examples.output: The logit and tuned lenses found no veto layer at the commitment token, because the fork has already happened at the first token; the community Jacobian lens for Qwen3-8B agreed with the next token less than the logit lens at every layer (0.104 against 0.291 at layer 27).

examples.input: circuits
examples.output: Path-patching circuits for the fork margin show a late stack of fork-position MLPs and heads carrying the fork logit in both families, but specificity fails at those sites under steering, DAS and cross-model patching; most matched random patching sets repeat a component, and the repaired layer-0 condition MLP gives about 7.9 nats on the five forced held-out prompts and about 0 on the five padded twins.

examples.input: plot a "path search algorithm" manifold, color each algorithm centroid by implemented-count (geodesic and mds; actual activation space)
examples.output: Geometry plots in actual activation coordinates exist from iterations 2 to 9, using geodesic distances, Isomap, MDS and centroids sized by implemented count, including four manifolds of the ten algorithms built with and without names in two models (iteration 9).

examples.input: then prohibit the top 5 in prompt, and see if the implemented count moves to the edge of those 5, or to the opposite side
examples.output: It depends on the map: unit-weight Dijkstra lies opposite the banned five on every manifold built from language (g 1.63, 1.20 and 1.08 times the median) and at the edge on the program manifold (0.67); its survivors place at the edge (15 of 15 on the primary frames, 10 of 15 on the programs-only frame) and the 15 Bellman-Ford/SPFA survivors opposite on both gate-passing Qwen3-32B frames. By mechanism the obeying model's survivors are mostly not renamed BFS by hand reads (0.30 unit-weight Dijkstra), and the exhaustion gap depends on the reading (Qwen3-32B by hand reads 0.30, by the runtime label 0.67).
